w: Under the auspices of the Swaminarayan Maha-mantra bicentenary celebration, a procession was carried out in the village of Sarangpur. A decorated float with sadhus and devotees devotionally chanting the Swaminarayan dhun weaved through the village. In the evening assembly, children from Dhandhuka performed a dance on the Maha-mantra bhajan. After some speeches, Swamishri blessed the assembly.
Swamishri performed the symbolic patotsav rituals of pujan and arti of Thakorji in the hari mandir. One hundred and fifty devotees participated in the mahapuja ritual.

Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha rituals of murtis for four BAPS Swaminaryan Mandirs for the villages of Haldava, Navapur, Kolhakui and Areth. Thereafter Swamishri blessed the devotees from these villages.

In the evening Swamishri blessed an assembly of 300 dignitaries who were mainly owners of sugar factories and leading social workers. On behalf of all the dignitaries Bhikhabhai N. Patel praised for Swamishri's services to society and thereafter presented Swamishri with a citation of honor.
Today, 68 years ago, Shastriji Maharaj had given diksha to Swamishri. After Swamishri’s morning puja, Ishwarcharan Swami garlanded and honoured Swamishri on behalf of everyone.

To please Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Guru Pramukh Swami Maharaj children, youths and senior devotees perform austerities, pilgrimages or other devotional means. The spiritual endeavors performed by the devotees during Swamishri's visit to the local centers are congratulatory and worthy of recognition. It also reflects Swamishri's divinity for inspiring such spiritual efforts in children, teenagers and devotees.
17 December 2006, Mumbai
Swamishri blessed 410 devotees from Bapunagar, 95 from Nikol and 15 from Saraspur suburbs for having pilgrimaged by foot and chanting the Swaminarayan mahamantra.
Two children, Haard and Mohlin, observed a waterless fast and performed dandvats from Asarwa suburb.
18 December 2006, Mumbai
Two devotees pilgrimaged 25 km by foot and also chanted the Janmangal Namavali from Gandhinagar.
20 December 2006, Mumbai
A youth, Varshil Shukla, performed dandvats from Maninagar suburb.
24 December 2006, Mumbai

Swamishri blessed 400 devotees who had walked from Ranip, 67 devotees who pilgrimaged 42 km by foot from Bavla, 50 devotees who pilgrimaged 18 km from Vanchh, 8 devotees who walked 15 km from Bilipura, 30 devotees from Gheekanta, 60 devotees from Nala and 50 employees of CTM and Madhu Industries textile mills in Amdavad.
25 December 2006, Mumbai

In Swamishri’s morning puja a total of 1,650 devotees pilgrimaged by foot from different suburbs of Amdavad, viz: 150 from Shahibaug, 200 from Naroda, 500 from Satellite, 30 from Subhash Bridge, 210 from Vadaj, 300 from Ghatlodia and Narayanpura, 250 from Sabarmati and Chandkheda, 6 from Science City and 6 from Sola Road.
28 December 2006, Mumbai
Devotees from Asarwa pilgrimaged by foot.
30 December 2006, Mumbai
Eleven youths pilgrimaged 13 km by foot from Odhav, and Vijaybhai performed dandvats from Raipur suburb.
31 December 2006, Mumbai
Ninety kishoris of Shahibaug sang 86 bhajans from 10 am to 4 pm.

Devotees pilgrimaged by foot from various suburbs, namely, 350 from Sola Road, 30 from Amraivadi, 75 employees of Madhu Industries and CTM, 175 from Krishnanagar, 125 from Chanakyapuri, 80 from Raipur, 65 from Bopal, 12 from Shahpur, and 15 devotees from Sanand (30 km).

ds.t: We must bow to the scholar
w: For the first time in the history of the Sampraday, Bhadresh Swami was receiving the D.Litt. degree. No one had received this degree before. In accordance with Pramukh Swami Maharaj's resolve, he had written a thesis in Sanskrit. Also, he had composed the Swaminarayan Bhashya (commentary) on the Prasthantrayi. It was for this commentary that he received this degree. Today he had come here, so he was honoured with a garland.
When he came to Swamishri and bowed at his feet, Swamishri at once said, "We must bow at the feet of one who is a scholar."
Swamishri's vision of glory touched everyone.
A sadhu phoned. He said, "I am late in congratulating you, but I want to congratulate you."
With natural carefree joy, Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "We are beyond congratulations. There is no birth and no death; we are of the form of bliss."
The sadhu said, "For you it is not like that, but we have to say it, don't we!"
Hearing this, Swamishri said, "All right, come on, now speak from the point of view of this world."
After some talk, Munitilak Swami came on the phone and said, "Happy birthday to you."
Hearing this, Swamishri said, "As I just told him, we are the atma, we are of the form of bliss."

A student studying at the hostel had committed a theft. Since he was caught stealing along with friends, the hostel managers had spoken to him somewhat strictly. After this incident, his father went to the sadhus and said many words that should not have been said, but later he repented. When Pramukh Swami Maharaj learnt of this, he had a call placed to him and, speaking with him, said, "You have told us the details. This should not have happened, but please overlook it. We ask your forgiveness."
Hearing such humility from Swamishri, the gentleman was choked with emotion and said, "Bapa! You should not ask forgiveness; I will fall into sin."

Saying this, he again began to tell in detail the incident that had happened, and in between Swamishri asked his forgiveness two or three times. Someone else makes the mistake, and Swamishri asks forgiveness! What forgiveness and humility Swamishri has!

Today, as Mahant Swami Maharaj was coming to his residence after the mangala arti at the mandir, dedicated youths of the organisation studying philosophy were standing there. They asked Swamishri, "There is a shibir in Sarangpur. We are going there. Would you like to come?"
"I am already there," Swamishri answered in the language of philosophy. In it was also a recognition of his all pervading form as Brahman.

Today, at the end of the morning puja, a dhun was sung that wove in the birthplaces of the guru parampara. In it Jabalpur was mentioned as Mahant Swami Maharaj's place. With reference to this, during breakfast the sadhus asked Swamishri, "By birthplace you would be called from Jabalpur. But some call you from Anand, and sing the dhun that way too. So where should we say you are from? Jabalpur or Anand?"
"From Akshardham," Swamishri said, laughing meaningfully.
Shriji Maharaj has said, "We have brought this Sadhu (the Gunatit Sant) and these disciplines from Akshardham." Today Swamishri too affirmed the same thing.

Today, during the meetings, Darshanbhai Patel of Vadodara came. The devotees who brought him began to explain before Mahant Swami Maharaj, "For the last 20 years Kalbhairav (a spirit) enters his body, and this causes great trouble. He has been shown to many people, but there is no result."

Their sentence had barely ended when the visitor's hands joined. His face turned. His hands, legs and body began to tremble. A tremor of fear spread through his words too. His words began to break... and trying to move away from Swamishri, he began to say, "I want to go, Maharaj! I want to go... I made a mistake, Maharaj! I made a mistake... I cannot look... I cannot look... give your blessings... I want to go... I want to go... give your blessings... I cannot look..."

The trembling and loudness of the speaker's voice slowly kept increasing. Then the sadhus saw that Swamishri, with unblinking eyes, was as if taking into his gaze this seeker and the Kalbhairav that had entered him. In that gaze there was radiance and piercing power. A sadhu opened a bottle of sanctified water and began sprinkling handfuls of the water on the visitor. Through the power of Swamishri's glance and the sanctified water, Darshanbhai at once became calm. He recovered. He was taken aside, seated and given water to drink. On his face there was peace and stability, because Kalbhairav had left his body forever.
"The servants of Hari always bring happiness, they make one fearless of the torment of Yama..." Today everyone experienced this in Swamishri.

Today, after blessing the Children's Day programme in the evening assembly, as Mahant Swami Maharaj was going to his residence, a boy named Akshar who had come from America recited: "By having darshan of such a Sadhu, the sins of the eyes are burnt..." Saying this, he asked Swamishri himself, "Swami! All my sins will be burnt, won't they?"
"By your darshan, others' sins are burnt," Swamishri said. Today everyone bathed in the splash of the boundless glory of devotees surging in his heart.

ds.t: The same mala for fifty five years
w: Tonight after the chesta, when talk turned to malas (rosaries), the sadhus said to Mahant Swami Maharaj, "When diksha was given in 1981, the sadhus were given malas costing 50 paise."

Confirming this, Swamishri said, "When we were given diksha, we were given a mala costing two annas. In it I have only changed the meru (head bead). It was just like the other beads, so I changed it."
For the last fifty five years Swamishri has turned the same mala in his morning puja. What simplicity! What non possessiveness!

ds.t: "The universes are seen, but not this"
w: Today, in view of the increased numbers, Kothari Karunamurtidas Swami came to ask Mahant Swami Maharaj for tomorrow's figure. His feeling was, "Swamishri is seated here and he knows everything. So if we do it by asking him, there will be no shortfall or excess."
He requested Swamishri to give the figure, but Swamishri began to laugh. Then he said slowly, "We wouldn't know. We have no experience, you see!"
Immediately the attendant sadhu took up the matter and said, "Why do you say that? You can see countless millions of universes, and you say no to this?"
"The universes are seen, but this is not seen," Swamishri said with a smile. Everyone burst out laughing.
